architecture.mechanism: Historical evolution of shunt valve designs with emphasis on failure mechanisms and patient-specific valve selection to prevent backflow and siphoning.
architecture.intervention: Adopt a passive, no-moving-parts, membrane-or-flap-free anti-siphon element modeled on fixed-orifice differential-pressure principles used in early shunt valve architectures (e.g., simple pressure-cracking geometry selected by hydrostatic head), integrated inline with the drip irrigation line to block reverse flow when the pump stops.
architecture.expected_effect: Eliminates backflow siphoning of irrigation water/fertilizer back through the line after pump shutdown, without requiring power or moving components, at low cost.
architecture.falsification_test: Bench-test the device on a drip irrigation rig with a 1 m elevation differential between supply reservoir and emitters; cycle the pump on/off 1000 times and measure any reverse volume passing the valve after shutdown. Pass criterion: zero measurable backflow volume per cycle. Compare against a control plain tube under identical head; the device must show backflow equal to or below a simple fixed-orifice reference.
